references.note: Read the King James Version of Paul’s account of distinct workers whose planting and watering depend upon growth given by God. Compare this Christian account of ministry with the compilation’s reed and seed images. Consider how responsibility for labor can be joined to humility about another person’s spiritual life.

subjects.displayTitle: The Concourse on High: companionship, witness, and service
subjects.introduction: To the children of martyred fathers ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes that they have not been left behind: condolences come from the Concourse on High, whose dwellers rejoice at a soul’s ascension even as they ask solace for those who grieve below. That is the first face of the heavenly company in the Bahá’í writings, consolation, and it is quickly joined by others. The Supreme Concourse, where Moses, Jesus, Elijah and the martyrs are said to dwell, prays for the faithful morning and evening, hears sighs no one else can hear, is drawn like a magnet to a gathering of two races, and is enraptured by music and collective praise. It is also a witness that laments wrongdoing, which turns the promise of companionship into a question of conduct: can one paint on the page of the world the ideal pictures of that celestial assembly? The epistle to the Hebrews pictures a kindred gathering of angels and perfected spirits, centered for Christians on Jesus and the new covenant [1]. The journey leads on toward the angels, the Kingdom of God, and the grace and confirmations that reach the visible world from the unseen.
subjects.arc: Begin with consolation and companionship, follow heavenly fellowship into conduct and service, then explore worship, covenant, remembrance, moral witness, and the hope of reunion.

order.why: Read the reported identification of supreme Souls and martyrs within the Concourse.
shortened: Hereupon another friend referred to the communing of Jesus on the Mount of Transfiguration with Moses and Elijah; and 'Abdu'l-Baha said: "The faithful are ever sustained by the presence of the Supreme Concourse. In the Supreme Concourse are Jesus, and Moses, and Elijah, and Baha'u'llah, and other supreme Souls: there, also, are the martyrs."

order.why: Open with assurance to the children of martyrs that they are not forsaken.
shortened: O remembrances of those resplendent spirits!

Although your distinguished fathers surrendered their souls in the field of glorious martyrdom, hastened away from the abyss of this sordid world of dust unto the lofty heights of the Abha Kingdom, and raised the banner of the most great bounty among the Concourse on high, ye have not been left behind, forsaken and lonely.

order.why: Read consolation for the bereaved alongside joy at a soul’s ascension.
shortened: However, for the passing of that glorious soul, condolences come from the Concourse on High, for the dwellers of the celestial realms rejoice at his ascension in the holy court, and they beseech solace for the grief-stricken of this world from the threshold of divine unity. His virtues are recorded and detailed in the Preserved Tablet and the unfurled scroll.

order.why: Consider the angel described as companion of the deprived.
shortened: The call of the Concourse on High is raised, and the angel of the Abha Kingdom is the companion of every deprived one.

order.why: Bring the inquiry immediately to the acquisition of virtues.
Keep illumination joined to righteousness and piety.
shortened: O thou servant of God! Hold thou firmly to the hem of the garment of righteousness and piety and to the utmost of thy ability seek thy illumination from the Concourse on High, from the Lamp of Guidance.
The stars shining in the firmament of the all-Merciful are characterised by this blessing of divine guidance.

order.why: Read the prayer for assistance through upright conduct and guidance.
Consider an interracial gathering as a magnet of spiritual confirmation.
Hear the reported challenge to portray heavenly ideals on the world’s page.
Describes a loving spiritual gathering as a reflection of the Heavenly Concourse.
Read the desire for purity and freedom from material attachment.
Keep the concise invitation to become one of the heavenly hosts.
shortened: Become one of the hosts of God and of the celestial angels.

order.why: Consider the varied descriptions of assistance through human form, spirit, and light.
shortened: O ye two bright stars in the horizon of the love of God!

The hosts of the Abha Kingdom at times appear in human form in the realm of contingency and render assistance to the Covenant and Testament, and at times they manifest as spirit and enter into pure mouths and speak forth, and at times they appear in the form of lights and illumine the horizons.

order.why: Retain the reported identification of guardian angels with divine powers.
Read the reported assistance associated with attaining the stated characteristics.
shortened: When they attain to these characteristics, the Hosts of the Supreme Concourse will assist them, and the confirmations of the Kingdom of Abha will surround them.

order.why: Consider consciousness stirred into movement through spiritual powers.
Read the explicit explanation of martial imagery as spreading divine fragrances and promoting the Covenant.
Keep the related battle-line metaphor in its spiritual setting.
Read the brief image of heavenly struggle alongside that explanation.
Retain the reported hosts awaiting someone’s entrance into the field.
shortened: The Supreme Concourse is descending. Today the hosts of the Supreme Concourse have assembled like unto armies made ready and they are waiting to see who will enter into the battle-field.

order.why: Keep the reported Grand Army identified with invisible angels.
Read the reported promise of assistance when threatened.
Consider the concise assurance of helpers and protectors.
shortened: The hosts of the Supreme Concourse are your helpers and the company of the near angels your protectors.

order.why: Read the promise of assistance to a particular person.
shortened: He is indeed of the people of Baha in the Kingdom of eternity, and the Concourse on High shall assist him.

order.why: Keep the invocation of heavenly aid in its prayerful voice.
Hear the recalled promise of aid for those who arise to serve.
Read the reported recollection of promised confirmations.
shortened: These have been from the promised confirmations of the Kingdom of God and the assistance of the invisible sovereignty of the Abha Beauty, which He has promised clearly in the verse, 'Verily, We behold you from Our realm of Glory, and shall aid whosoever will arise for the triumph of Our Cause with the hosts of the Concourse on high and a company of Our favored angels.'

order.why: Consider mercy and successive hosts through the sea image.
shortened: The ocean of the Most Great Mercy is surging and the hosts of the Concourse on High are advancing wave upon wave.

order.why: Read remembrance and spiritual quickening as occasions for heavenly pride.
Consider the source’s portrayal of holy souls yearning to serve on earth.
Read the reported table prayer asking that those present become life-giving.
shortened: O Lord! Make this food heavenly and make those assembled here of the hosts of Thy Supreme Concourse so that they may become life-giving and the cause of the enlightenment of the world of man, that they may arise to, guide all the peoples of the world.

order.why: Consider a homeland becoming an example of the heavenly company.
shortened: Make all intoxicated with the wine of alast and give them free rein in the arena of the love of God, so that the homeland of the Greatest Name - may my spirit be sacrificed for His loved ones - may become an example of the Supreme Concourse and manifest the light of the Abha Kingdom.

order.why: Read building the edifice as an enduring service that brings joy.
Enter the House of Worship through collective prayer, music, and rejoicing.
shortened: The Mashriqu'l-Adhkar is the dawning-place of lights and the gathering place of the righteous. Whenever a company of noble souls assemble in a heavenly gathering there and offer supplications, intone divine verses, and chant prayers with wondrous melodies, the inmates of the Concourse on high hearken and call out, crying, "Happy are we; let all the world rejoice!" for, praise be unto God, souls from among the angels of the Kingdom of Glory have arisen in the nether world to commune with their Lord and intone the verses of Divine Unity in a gathering of holiness.

order.why: Read music as a praiseworthy science serving praise and worship.
shortened: O servant of Baha! Music is regarded as a praiseworthy science at the Threshold of the Almighty, so that thou mayest chant verses at large gatherings and congregations in a most wondrous melody and raise such hymns of praise at the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar to enrapture the Concourse on High.

order.why: Keep Barbad and the psalms of David within the invitation to uplifting music.
shortened: O bird of the meadow! Begin with a melody to sing a love-song that will cause the dwellers of the Supreme Concourse to be stirred into motion.
In gatherings and meetings, play and sing with the melody of Barbad and the psalms of David, that the angels of the Supreme Concourse may experience joy and delight and obtain spiritual happiness.

order.why: Consider the reported desire for a melody with enduring effects.
Read the brief invitation to melodies that stir spiritual joy.
Hear the prayer for a voice attuned to heavenly airs.
Read praise and the proclamation of servitude through the dove image.
shortened: By the True One! The ears of the Concourse on High hearken to thy melodies in glorification and praise, as thou extollest thy Lord, the Most Glorious.

Therefore, ascend to the Kingdom and warble like the dove of holiness in the gardens of the realm of might, glorifying the Lord of grandeur and the divine realm, the Most Glorious Luminary, and proclaiming my servitude to that exalted Threshold before which the Concourse on High bow down their radiant faces.

order.why: Consider the faithful singing together as an occasion for heavenly thanksgiving.
shortened: Know ye verily that the denizens of the Realm on High, the dwellers in the habitations of Glory, laud and glorify the company of the faithful on earth, who raise their voice with one accord and sing the praise of the Lord and magnify His holy Name.

order.why: Read the garden’s birds and life-giving melodies as images of unity and praise.
shortened: The birds of the rose garden and meadow raise a new strain at every moment, and with every breath a life-giving melody from the birds of the garden reaches the ears of every mindful one - the song of glorification and sanctification, and the melody of unity and praise that reaches the Abha Kingdom and brings the Supreme Concourse to delight and rapture, joy and ecstasy.

order.why: Keep the song that awakens sleepers within this sequence of music.
shortened: It is the song of the nightingales that reacheth to heaven's zenith, and the melody of the birds that awakeneth the slumberers.

order.why: Read the prayer for awakened sight and hearing with its preserved source omission.
Hear the brief invitation to listen and glorify.
shortened: As to thee: Listen to the Supreme Concourse and hear the call, "Glory be unto my Lord, the El-Baha!"

order.why: Keep the answering cry of praise.
Read the leviathan and ocean imagery beside the Concourse’s song.
Consider the source’s account of tablets chanted forever.
shortened: What tablet could be more preserved than that Preserved Tablet, what scroll more widely proclaimed than that Book? The denizens of the Abha Kingdom and the Supreme Concourse will chant and sing those tablets forever.

order.why: Read the request for the torch of mercy and flourishing meetings.
shortened: Even as moths shall the birds of the gardens of divine unity circle in adoration round this light and through the reality of God's essential unity shall thy meetings be made to flourish.
Beseech thou God that He kindle within thee the torch of His mercy and enable thee to shine brightly in the company of the Concourse.

order.why: Consider radiance that grows toward the heavenly world.
Keep love joined to successive spiritual messages.
Read guidance through brightened eyes, hearing, and a gladdened heart.
Consider Gabriel as intermediary in the source’s account of revelation.
shortened: O messenger of the love of God! Gabriel in the court of the Glorious Lord is a favored angel and an honored servant, for he is the supreme intermediary for the descent of the revelation of the Glorious Lord, and he illumines the hearts of the righteous with the lights of divine bounty.

order.why: Read the invocation of Gabriel through questions recalling revelation and divine power.
Keep the cleansing of the heart beside listening to Gabriel’s melodies.
shortened: Such a soul would banish the Evil One and all his machinations from the sanctuary of the heart and would enable the ears of men to be attuned to the melodies of Gabriel.

order.why: Retain the reported newspaper comparison as figurative language.
shortened: The subscribers to this newspaper are frail humanity but the subscribers to that newspaper are the angels of the supreme Concourse.

order.why: Read the reported story of angels and Azrael in its narrative setting.
Keep the reported heavenly cities in the speaker’s dialogue.
Read the reported images of Moses’ fire, mercy’s clouds, and glad tidings.
Consider steadfastness and service as reasons for heavenly thanksgiving.
shortened: The Concourse on High uttereth praise for every soul steadfast and firm in God's Covenant, and giveth thanks for every diffuser of the fragrances of God, glorifying their Lord morning and evening, and praising Him for having raised up from among His servants such men whom neither the affairs of creation, nor doubts, nor uncertain matters can distract from the manifest Light, the Straight Path, and the Ancient Horizon.

order.why: Read prayer for those whom blame cannot turn from the Covenant.
shortened: O thou who art turned unto the Most Glorious Kingdom! By God, the True One! Verily the tribes of the Supreme Concourse offer prayers for those who are firm in the Covenant of God, and they aid those servants whom no blame from any blamer can deter from remaining steadfast in the Testament of God.

order.why: Keep firmness, effort, and the spreading of light together.
shortened: O thou who art firm in the Covenant and Testament by a power from the highest horizon! By God the True One, verily the people of the Most Glorious Kingdom pray for thee in the heaven of eternity, and the dwellers of the pavilions of the Realm of Might speak in praise of thy firmness in the Covenant of God, thy steadfastness in His Cause, thy striving for the diffusion of His light, the rising of His sun, the manifestation of His signs, the penetration of His Word, and the spreading of His traces.

order.why: Read the Covenant’s adherents addressed as watched from above.
shortened: O ye who are holding fast unto the Covenant and Testament! This day, from the realms of the All-Glorious, from the Kingdom of Holiness where hosannas of glorification and praise rise up, the Company on high direct their gaze upon you.

order.why: Consider the parallel image of heavenly attention.
Read steadfastness as an occasion for gladness.
shortened: Today the Concourse on High is delighted by the glad tidings of the steadfastness and firmness of the friends.

order.why: Keep the personal praise of a faithful handmaiden.
shortened: By God the True One, verily the holy angels give you glad tidings from the Supreme Concourse, saying: "Well done, well done, O handmaiden of God, in that you have been faithful to the Covenant, believed in God, and been attracted by the fragrances of God!"

order.why: Read congratulations for guidance and turning toward God.
Keep the related blessing in its personal address.
shortened: By Your life, the Concourse on High calls out to you: "Blessed are you, then blessed again, for this supreme guidance and this gift whose lights shine forth upon all regions!"

order.why: Read the resounding congratulations throughout created things.
shortened: By God the One alone Beloved! Verily, the call "Well done!" and again, "Well done" hath been raised by the Concourse on High and the cry "Great is your blessedness, doubly great your happiness!" is heard loud and clear from within the realities of all created things.

order.why: Retain the personal assurance of intercession and praise.
shortened: By the righteousness of the Lord! The angels of holiness intercede for thee in the Abha of Kingdom, and the Concourse on high cry out most loudly unto thee saying: "Well done, well done!

order.why: Keep the brief praise for attaining a blessing.
shortened: By thy life, the Concourse on High praise thee and cry out thy name for attaining such a great blessing.

order.why: Read the source’s thanksgiving for the designated Center of the Covenant.
shortened: O spiritual friends! The denizens of the Supreme Concourse and dwellers of the Most Glorious Kingdom loosed their tongues in thanksgiving for the favors at the dawn of the Covenant and bowed their heads in prostration at the Sacred Threshold, saying: "O Kind Lord! Praise and glory be unto Thee for having designated the Specific Center and made the Center of the Covenant renowned throughout all regions.

order.why: Consider the Covenant described as a firm foundation.
shortened: O ye who are firm in the Covenant!

The Incomparable Lord shed the light of His Covenant upon all horizons and made such a binding agreement that it brought the Concourse on High into a state of joy and rapture. All arose in thanksgiving to the Ancient Beauty, praising: "Glory be to God that He hath made His Cause firm and established His Covenant as the mightiest foundation!"

order.why: Keep the source’s reference to the primal world of atoms in its theological register.
shortened: Thus did the faces of the people of the Most Glorious Kingdom beam with joy and the hearts of the Concourse on High were gladdened. They loosened their tongues in prayer and spoke in praise of their Lord, the Lord of the highest heavens, saying: "Glory be to our Most Glorious Lord Who took the Covenant in the primal world of atoms and blessed be His name in the next creation."

order.why: Read the prayer’s movement from dust through nurture, guidance, and steadfastness.
Hear the handmaiden’s prayerful affirmation of signs, proof, and covenant.
shortened: O Lord! This is Thy handmaiden who hath believed in Thee and in Thy signs, who hath been assured of Thy proof and Thy Covenant, who hath accepted Thy words, who hath circled round the Spot round which circle the Concourse on High, and who hath turned toward the Kingdom of Abha.

order.why: Read the invitation to attach oneself to the heavenly company.
shortened: Therefore, if thou seekest the supernal world and desirest the Kingdom of wealth, set thine eyes upon the horizon of Abha and attach thyself to the Concourse on high that thou mayest possess never-ending honor and witness boundless glory and exaltation.

order.why: Consider the arrayed Kingdom and joy of attainment.
Keep praise and rejoicing in their devotional setting.
shortened: The sounds of glorification and magnification have been raised from the Supreme Concourse - glory be to my Most Glorious Lord! - and those near to God are in great joy.

order.why: Read the blessing associated with the countenances of the faithful.
shortened: By God, the inmates of Paradise and the concourse of those who have drawn nigh are blessed by their countenances.

order.why: Consider those numbered among the Concourse and the hope of shining faces.
Read trustworthiness as the responsibility accompanying a lofty station.
shortened: When he reacheth that lofty station and this exalted homeland, it behooveth him to be trustworthy with the treasuries of God's knowledge and reliable with the pearls of His wisdom's mysteries. He must be a guardian of these divine teachings deposited in the vessels of illumined hearts by God, the Creator of all beings.

order.why: Keep the marketplace image as an invitation to assess what is spiritually precious.
Read forgiveness and the particular grace associated with entering the sacred land.
Keep the blessing of pilgrimage to the sacred Spot.
Read the personal hope of attaining pilgrimage.
shortened: My hope is that you and Jinab-i-Bayda will succeed in circumambulating the gathering place of the Supreme Concourse.

order.why: Hear the glad tidings addressed to a seeker of pilgrimage.
Consider thanksgiving for being drawn near to a supreme grace.
shortened: O thou who art mentioned by My Most Exalted Pen! Render thanks unto God for having enabled thee to attain unto this supreme grace and for having drawn thee nigh unto this station round which circle the Concourse on High and His honored servants.

order.why: Keep the blessing upon women who turn their hearts toward the divine station.
shortened: The glory be upon thee and upon those women who have heard and turned with their hearts toward a station round which circle the Concourse on High and the dwellers of this glorious station.

order.why: Read the House’s exalted station within its own sacred geography.
shortened: Praise be to God Who hath raised His House to such a station that the Concourse on High and the denizens of the Kingdom of Names have circumambulated it, and hath made it the point of adoration for the world and the sanctuary round which the peoples circle.

order.why: Keep the station visited by the angels and Concourse.
Read the particular remembrance of an Afnan and attainment of the sacred Spot.
Consider glory and adoration in the brief address.
Read revelation’s purpose of being read with gratitude.
shortened: The Book speaks with the tongue of revelation at this Most Great Scene - this station round which circle the Concourse on High and the dwellers of the cities of eternity and the inhabitants of the Most Exalted Kingdom, that men might read and be thankful.

order.why: Keep the procession of spirits and the Youth in its visionary narrative.
shortened: All spirits gathered to behold the Beauty from this noble vantage. Not a single soul or spirit or manifestation remained behind the veil of the Divine Essence or the coverings of the Almighty Dominion - all descended from their stations to witness this glorious Beauty. The Youth walked forth and with Him walked the spirits of the near ones and the angels of all worlds, until He stood before the Steed.

order.why: Read the sea and Ark image as a scene of heavenly rapture.
Consider the Concourse’s circumambulation and reverence for the remembered Figure.
shortened: O Khalil! The Glorious One has come and the Son has gone to the place of sacrifice and did not return, and gave up His spirit and all He had in the path of God, the Lord of Lords. By God's life, He turned with a face by which earth and heaven were illumined, as the Creator of Names bears witness to this in this mighty station. By God's life, the Concourse on High circled round Him and every trustworthy Messenger sought blessing from His dust.

order.why: Read verses from imprisonment described as enrapturing the heavenly company.
Consider thanksgiving for revelation encompassing all things.
shortened: In this day the Concourse on High and the dwellers of the Most Exalted Paradise are all engaged in praise and thanksgiving to God, inasmuch as the lights of His Revelation have encompassed all things.

order.why: Read certitude and rejection through the source’s contrasting images.
shortened: Glory be unto those who have cast behind them vain imaginings, turning their faces toward the horizon whence hath shone the Sun of Certitude through this Name, whereby the Concourse on High rejoiced and every rejected satan lamented.

order.why: Keep the contrast between heavenly rejoicing and human unawareness.
shortened: O Muhammad! The Day of praise and thanksgiving has come, wherein the Concourse on High rejoices, yet most of the people are as dead.

order.why: Read circumambulation of the Throne alongside the warning of error.
shortened: This is a Day wherein the Concourse on High circle round the Throne of God, the Lord of all beings and the Master of the Hereafter and of the former times, yet most of the people are in manifest error.

order.why: Consider the source’s regret over human hesitation before revelation.
shortened: Had the people known, they would not have cast the Command of God behind their backs, nor would they have hesitated in this Cause, unto which have turned the Concourse on High and the dwellers of Paradise and those whom none knoweth save God, the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: Read the visionary scene of prostration, breath, song, and warning.
shortened: At this moment all who are in the heavens and on earth prostrated themselves before God, and the Holy Spirit breathed into the temples of the Concourse on High, and the Dove warbled in the midmost heart of eternity, and all necks bowed down before His command, while the proud were in the fire of hell and grievous peril, and verily He was witness over all things.

order.why: Bring attentive ears and all-seeing eyes into moral witness.
shortened: The Concourse on High hath attentive ears and the eyes of God are all-seeing.

order.why: Read the forceful rebuke of wrongdoing and self-deception.
shortened: In this Day the Concourse on high beholdeth you in your evil doings and shunneth your company, and yet ye perceive it not.  They ask of one another:  "What words do these fools utter, and in what valley are they wont to graze?  Do they deny that whereunto their very souls testify, and shut their eyes to that which they plainly behold?"

order.why: Keep the source’s dissociation from those who turn away in its own voice.
Read heavenly lament over human actions.
shortened: They have perpetrated in this Revelation that which hath caused the Concourse on High to lament and the denizens of Paradise to cry out from their glorious station.

order.why: Consider the source’s image of interrupted spiritual breezes and shaken pillars.
shortened: And thereby shall the breezes of the Spirit be cut off from the direction of the horizons, and the pillars of the concourse of the exalted ones shall be shaken.

order.why: Read the desire to share tribulation in its devotional and historical register.
Keep the related wish to have shared the faithful’s attainment.
shortened: The Concourse on High uttereth this most exalted word: "Would that we had been with them and attained that which none among the servants hath attained!"

order.why: Consider souls whose coming is eagerly awaited.
shortened: These are the souls whose existence the denizens of the Supreme Concourse take pride in and whose presence they eagerly anticipate.

order.why: Read the welcoming of an ascended spirit.
shortened: By God! When his spirit ascended, the Concourse on High welcomed him and found from him the fragrance of the garment of thy Most Glorious Lord, and they ascended with him to the Supreme Companion.

order.why: Keep the related welcome and its acknowledgment of beings known only to God.
shortened: By God! When he turned, the Concourse on High welcomed him, then those whom none knoweth save God, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

order.why: Read a departed brother remembered as still mindful of the addressee.
Retain the reported explanation of heavenly welcome within its source.
shortened: It is called the Heavenly body, and this is what is meant by Christ, when He says, that after leaving this body man enters the Kingdom; It is beyond the human Kingdom. This is what is meant by Baha'0'Llah when He says: 'The Supreme Concourse welcomes you'.

order.why: Consider rest described as ascension and nearness.
shortened: Its stillness is ascension to the Supreme Concourse and its rest is nearness to the precincts of the Most Great Mercy.

order.why: Read the concise assurance of morning and evening prayers.
shortened: Blessed is the lowly one who hath shown humility in My days,

and the servant who advanceth to serve My loved ones who, through utterance, aid the Cause of their Lord, the Merciful, in the cities and lands. They are My loved ones in My earth and My servants among My creatures. The Concourse on High pray for them at morn and eventide.

order.why: Keep the parallel invocation of the heavenly company’s prayers.
shortened: Upon them pray the Concourse on High and those who circle round the Throne, by the command of One Who is the Ordainer, the All-Wise.

order.why: Consider remembrance and prayers for a particular person.
shortened: The denizens of the Supreme Paradise make mention of him, and upon him do the angels and the Spirit shower their prayers, from the presence of the Mighty, the All-Bestowing.

order.why: Read the specific remembrance of Aqa Muhammad-Javad Farhad.
Keep the personal blessing of a name remembered above.
shortened: O 'Abdu'l-Husayn! Your name is blessed and beloved, and is mentioned in the Concourse on High.

order.why: Read the Tablet’s remembrance extending to the heavenly company.
Close with remembrance witnessed by the Concourse and those around the exalted Seat.

questions: What changes when the Concourse on High is approached through consolation, prayer, and companionship rather than imagery alone?
Which virtues do the passages associate with heavenly fellowship, and how might these appear in ordinary relationships?
How do music, collective worship, and interracial fellowship connect the visible community with the unseen world in these readings?
How does Hebrews’ heavenly assembly compare with this compilation, and what distinctive role does Jesus retain in that Christian passage?
How might the images of heavenly witness and lament deepen reflection on the effects of our conduct?
What possibilities do the passages on remembrance and the departed offer for sustaining both hope and care for people who are grieving?

references.note: Read the King James Version’s gathering of angels, the heavenly assembly, and perfected spirits. Compare its sense of belonging beyond the visible world with the compilation’s companionship and worship. Retain the passage’s distinct Christian center in Jesus as mediator of the new covenant.
